title: Kimi K3 on MI355X (Wafer blog)
brief: Wafer benchmarked Moonshot's 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3 on AMD's MI355X (288GB VRAM per GPU): 952 tok/s/node aggregate and 118 tok/s single-stream — over 3.8× the per-node throughput of a 2-node B200 deployment. With the MI355X ~2.4× cheaper per GPU than NVIDIA's B300, it wins decisively on performance per dollar; the post also details real ROCm fixes, including speculative decode via RadixArk's DSpark draft and zero-padding heads to unlock the AITER MLA prefill kernel. All throughput figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: All throughput figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
details: Wafer blog post "Is memory the moat?" on serving Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters, over 1.5TB of VRAM before KV cache) on AMD MI355X GPUs instead of NVIDIA Blackwell. On a 1024-token in / 400-token out benchmark, 8x MI355X reached 952 tok/s per node aggregate and 118 tok/s single-stream decode — over 3.8x the aggregate per node of a 2-node B200 setup and the best performance per dollar of the three configs tested, at roughly 2.4x cheaper per GPU-hour than B300. The post details the engineering: speculative decoding via RadixArk's DSpark draft (fixing a missing top_k_renorm_prob definition in sglang's ROCm path) and a head-count padding fix (12 to 16) to unlock AITER's fast MLA prefill kernel, speeding prefill 2 to 3x. Their takeaway: with agents closing the kernel gap, the CUDA moat is eroding.
